text: Why do the nations rage, and the peoples plot in vain?
The kings of the earth take their stand, and the rulers conspire together against the LORD and against his Anointed:
"Let us tear off their fetters and fling their cords away from us!"

versions.text: "Let us break their chains and throw off their ropes!"
versions.explanation: The Hebrew includes "from us" (mimmennu), which the current wording leaves out, and the paired verbs "tear off"/"fling away" carry the defiant force of the original more vividly for oral reading.

text: He who sits enthroned in heaven laughs; the Lord mocks them.
Then he speaks to them in his anger and terrifies them in his wrath:
"I myself have installed my king on Zion, my holy mountain."
I will proclaim the LORD's decree. He said to me: "You are my Son; today I have begotten you.
Ask of me, and I will make the nations your inheritance, the ends of the earth your possession.
You will break them with an iron rod and shatter them like a potter's jar."
So now, you kings, be wise; be warned, you judges of the earth.
Serve the LORD with fear, and rejoice with trembling.

Kiss the Son, or he will be angry and you will perish on the way, for his wrath can flare up in a moment. Blessed are all who take refuge in him. [footnote: The word rendered "Son" here (Hebrew bar) is the Aramaic form; the phrase is difficult, and some understand it as "pay homage sincerely" or "kiss his feet."]

versions.text: Kiss the Son, or he will be angry and you will perish on the way, for his wrath can flare up in a moment. Blessed are all who take refuge in him.
versions.explanation: The reading "Kiss the Son" rests on a rare Aramaic form and is textually disputed. A brief footnote would help readers without altering the rendering, which reads well aloud.
